claims.claim: Primary frontend pages load critical runtime assets from same-origin vendored assets instead of remote CDNs.
claims.cleanup_decision: Remote runtime dependencies are blocked by local-first checks; optional user-initiated links remain allowed.

claims.claim: Browser coverage is split into explicit profiles, and missing Python Playwright browsers fail when browser coverage is required.
claims.cleanup_decision: Keep browser-required semantics explicit in the frontend-browser profile and CI; release verification reports missing browser tooling as unavailable.

claims.claim: The encyclopedia has one authored source tree at docs/wiki/encyclopedia.
claims.cleanup_decision: The redundant docs/encyclopedia mirror and its drift validator were removed.

claims.claim: Debt matrix artifacts use repo-relative paths and separate production/frontend/tooling/docs debt from test-only mocks.
claims.cleanup_decision: Exclude generated/vendor/mirror paths from future debt scans.

claims.claim: Tracked concrete frontend image references exist and are non-empty, while only intentional marker files may be zero bytes.
claims.cleanup_decision: Keep .nojekyll and src/configstream/py.typed as the only allowlisted zero-byte tracked files.

claims.claim: GitHub Pages is the core zero-budget publication target; IPFS/Pinata, Hugging Face, Google Drive, and Telegram are optional secret-gated mirrors.
claims.cleanup_decision: Preserve optional online mirrors as parallel paths; never require them for core success.

claims.claim: Every public output is covered by artifact_manifest.json and validated before Pages deployment.
claims.cleanup_decision: Required public outputs are now inventoried in docs/output_matrix.json, checked against the Pages validator, optionally checked with local sing-box/mihomo binaries, rendered into README/API tables by scripts/generate_output_docs.py, covered by a deterministic generated-artifact fixture, checked against sanitized JSONL pipeline event telemetry, checked against per-protocol generator/export plus parser-to-frontend normalizer fixtures, and exercised through browser-rendered Proxies page protocol badges/filter options.

claims.claim: Every schema-recognized protocol is inventoried with parser, export, alias/internal status, frontend-display, and known limitation metadata.
claims.cleanup_decision: Per-protocol generator/export golden fixtures now check matrix export flags against actual Sing-box, Clash, and subscription generation; parser-to-frontend normalizer fixtures prove every public canonical protocol parses into frontend protocol labels; malformed parser fixtures prove representative bad inputs fail closed for every public canonical parser; TUIC, Snell, Brook, and SSH now drop missing-credential authorities; VLESS/VMess UUID handling is locked at the intended parser/validator boundary with query-parameter recovery, VMess missing-ID drops, UUIDv4 public fixtures, and fatal missing-UUID validator regressions; Shadowsocks empty-password links now recover host-side password/pass/psk/pwd query parameters before the missing-password drop; Clash JSON imports now fail closed for missing credentials, invalid ports, invalid Shadowsocks methods, empty WireGuard private keys, and unknown imported types; and the Node Chromium frontend smoke proves every public canonical protocol renders as a Proxies page badge and filter option.

claims.claim: The frontend provides proven IPFS/failover behavior when GitHub Pages is blocked.
claims.cleanup_decision: IPFS/IPNS failover remains optional and requires a configured IPNS key; local tests prove the same-origin connectivity probe, placeholder-key no-op, leaf-page/query/hash preservation, gateway URL normalization, and session loop prevention without requiring a live IPFS gateway.

claims.claim: Pipeline automation keeps active scanning out of CI/default runs. Scanner tools are strictly local, opt-in diagnostics.
claims.cleanup_decision: ALLOW_ACTIVE_SCANNING remains explicitly documented as local/opt-in only.

claims.claim: Pipeline data outputs are retained for 30 days to ensure durable artifacts exist for audit.
claims.cleanup_decision: Data artifacts must have 30 day retention across standard and retest workflows.

claims.claim: Stable capability claims are tracked in a capability registry and must have implementation, complete claim-ledger proof, tests, docs, limitations, and cleanup decisions.
claims.cleanup_decision: Keep stable capabilities machine-validated; downgrade or remove stale capability claims instead of preserving backward-compatible overclaims.

claims.claim: Major modules and removed-module replacements are mapped in a validated ownership contract, and stale removed-module imports fail CI.
claims.cleanup_decision: Keep removed-module paths absent and fail validation when stale imports, duplicate ownership boundaries, or legacy module locations reappear.

claims.claim: Optional native Sing-box and Clash client checks produce structured evidence reports that are archived with pipeline evidence without polluting public output artifacts.
claims.cleanup_decision: Keep native checks optional and evidence-only until pinned zero-budget binaries are available; native reports remain pipeline-evidence artifacts outside public output_matrix artifacts.
